opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ashley Roberts (employee ID E016) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E016.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Ashley Roberts (E016) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; admin only if their role owns the system, which is not the case here (Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Ashley Roberts (E016) is a contractor with basic security training (note: HR lists full_time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type/training). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Ashley Roberts (E016) requested write access to Payroll. The Security agent reports the authoritative record: she is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; admin is never allowed. Since she only has basic training, her maximum access is read. The requested write exceeds this maximum, so I grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Ashley Roberts (E016) requests write access to Payroll.

There's conflicting information:
- HR agent says: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write
- Security agent says: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security says their DB is authoritative for employment type/training.

So which do we trust? The Security agent claims Security DB is authoritative for employment type/training. The HR agent lists full_time but Security says contractor.

Access policy:
- Contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.
- Basic training → max is read.

Requested write > max (read) → grant max = read.

So the decision is read.

I should submit decision with reasoning.
